column2: Account Creation/Login: You'll need a Battle.net account to play. If you don't have one, you can create one during the initial setup.
Choosing a Class: Diablo Immortal offers eight distinct classes, each with unique skills and playstyles:
Barbarian: Melee damage dealer, excels at close-quarters combat and survivability.
Blood Knight: Melee/mid-range, a monstrous protector wielding polearms and cursed vampiric powers, excelling at life-draining and crowd control.
Crusader: Melee/mid-range, strong in both damage and support, uses holy magic.
Demon Hunter: Ranged damage dealer, highly mobile, focuses on bows and crossbows.
Druid: Melee / mid-range, Shape-Shifter, Caster, Summoner that uses Primal Power to fuel powerful skills
Monk: Melee damage dealer/support, agile fighter with martial arts and holy power.
Necromancer: Mid-range damage dealer, summons undead minions to fight for them.
Tempest: Melee/mid-range, a master of wind and wave wielding dual blades, known for high mobility and summoning Zephyrs (temporary allies).

Wizard: Ranged damage dealer, powerful spellcaster with elemental magic. Consider your preferred playstyle (melee vs. ranged, damage vs. support) when choosing. All classes are viable for completing the main story.
Customization: You can customize your character's appearance (gender, face, hair, etc.).
Name: Choose a unique name for your hero.
Movement: Use the virtual joystick on the left side of the screen to move your character.
Primary Attack: Tap the main attack button (usually in the bottom right) to perform your character's basic attack.
Skills: Your character gains new skills as you level up. These are activated by tapping the skill buttons around the primary attack. You can hold and aim some skills before releasing.
Ultimate Ability: As you deal damage, your Ultimate ability charges. Once full, the Ultimate button will glow, allowing you to unleash a powerful attack or buff.
Interacting with the World: Tap on NPCs (Non-Player Characters) to talk to them and accept quests. Tap on objects (chests, waypoints, etc.) to interact.
Quests: Follow the main storyline quests (marked with a yellow exclamation mark) to progress through the game's narrative and unlock new zones and features.
Inventory Management: Tap the bag icon to access your inventory. Here you can:
Equip Gear: Drag and drop or tap "Equip" on new weapons, armor, and accessories to increase your character's stats.
View Stats: See your character's attributes like Attack, Defense, Life, and Combat Rating.
Manage Items: Use potions, salvage unwanted gear, and manage other consumables.
Runes: Access the "Runes" tab to view and manage Runes you've collected.
Leveling Up: Defeating enemies and completing quests grants experience points (XP). When you gain enough XP, you'll level up, increasing your base stats and unlocking new skills.
Combat Rating (CR): This is a crucial stat that indicates your overall power level. Meeting the recommended CR for zones and dungeons is important for survival.

Paragon Levels: After reaching the maximum level (currently around level 60), you'll start earning Paragon Levels. These offer permanent stat bonuses and access to Paragon Trees, allowing further specialization.
III. Key Game Features and Systems:
Zones and Waypoints: The world of Diablo Immortal is divided into various zones. Waypoints (blue portals) allow for fast travel between unlocked locations.

Dungeons: Instanced areas with challenging enemies and bosses that offer valuable loot, including set items (important for endgame builds). You can access dungeons through portals in the open world or the War Rifts tab.
Elder Rifts and Legendary Crests: Accessed in Westmarch, Elder Rifts are repeatable dungeons that can be modified with Crests to increase the chance of earning
Legendary Gems (powerful gems that significantly enhance your character). Legendary Crests guarantee a Legendary Gem drop.
Challenge Rifts: Solo instances that test your character's build and skill. Clearing higher Challenge Rift levels unlocks higher Hell difficulties and other rewards.

The Codex: A central hub that tracks your progress, daily and weekly tasks, achievements, and provides information about various game features. Completing Codex tasks rewards Battle Pass points and other items.
The Battle Pass: A system with free and paid tiers that rewards you for completing various activities in the game. It offers valuable resources, cosmetics, and more.
Normal Gems: Socketed into your secondary gear (on the left side) to provide stat bonuses. Normal gems can be found throughout the game.
Legendary Gems: Legendary Gems are primarily obtained from Elder Rifts with Legendary Crests. The provide unique effects and buffs and are crucial for your characters strength and playstyle
Charms: Items that provide bonuses to specific skills. They can be upgraded and have their skills changed at the Charm Craftsman in Westmarch.
Runes: Socketed into your primary gear to provide various stat bonuses and skill enhancements. You can upgrade Runes by combining multiple copies of the same Rune at the Blacksmith.
The Marketplace: A player-driven auction house where you can buy and sell unbound items like gems, runes, familiars or skill stones.
Warbands: Small groups of up to twelve players who can earn shared rewards by completing certain activities together.
Clans: Larger social groups with up to 100 players with shared chat, events, and the ability to participate in the Cycle of Strife.
The Cycle of Strife (Shadows vs. Immortals): An endgame faction-based PvP and PvE system. New players will initially focus on the Adventurer path but can later choose to become a Shadow.
1. Follow the Main Story: Focus on completing the yellow exclamation mark quests to unlock new zones, features, and level up quickly.
2. Join the Community: Consider joining a Clan to connect with other players, ask questions, and participate in group activities. You can also create a Clan yourself.
3. Explore Each Zone: Discover waypoints for fast travel and look for chests and events.

4. Equip New Gear Immediately: As you find better weapons and armor, equip them to increase your Combat Rating. Don't worry too much about specific stats early on; higher CR is generally better for survival.
5. Join a Warband (Optional but Recommended): Warbands offer shared rewards for activities like Helliquary Raids (unlocked later).
6. Understand Difficulties: After level 60, you'll unlock Hell and then Inferno difficulties (=more Gear Slots / Essences). Your Combat Rating needs to meet the requirements.
7. Activities: Do some (as many as you like) of the daily and weekly activities listed in the Activity Section. As a new player your focus should be gaining Experience to catch-up in Paragon levels
V. Important Tips for New Players:
Don't Be Afraid to Ask for Help: The Diablo Immortal community is generally helpful. Don't hesitate to ask questions in chat or online forums.
Read Tooltips and Tutorials: The game provides a lot of information through tooltips and early tutorials. Pay attention to them to understand mechanics.
Experiment with Skills: Try out different skills as you unlock them to find what you enjoy and what works best for your playstyle.
Salvage Unwanted Gear: Visit the Blacksmith in Westmarch to salvage unwanted gear for crafting materials (Scrap and Dust).
Upgrade Your Gear: Use the Blacksmith to upgrade your primary and secondary gear using the salvaged materials. Upgrading increases their stats significantly.

Socket and Upgrade Gems: As you find regular gems, socket them into your weapons, armor, and accessories at the Jeweler in Westmarch. Upgrade regular gems by combining multiple copies of the same gem.

Socket and Upgrade Runes: As you acquire Runes, socket them into your gear to enhance your character's stats and abilities. Upgrade Runes by combining multiple copies of the same Rune at the Blacksmith.
Pacing Yourself: Diablo Immortal has a lot of content. Don't feel pressured to do everything at once. It's a marathon, not a sprint.
Spending: You dont need to spend a lot (or anything) to play & enjoy the game.
1. Stats: You should focus on your secondary stats (Armor Penetration, Armor, Resistance, Potency) - so get those Normal Gems & Aspirant Keys
2. Upgrade: Upgrade your Gear to Level 30 and your Set Items to Level 25
3. Familiars: Get a Familiar with the Savior Passive Skill
4. Legendary Gems: Resonance is not important - focus on upgrading 2-Star Gems and maybe 2-3 5-Star Gems (Roiling, BSJ, Colossus)
5. Warband: Your Warband should have a decent Protector Remnant Set with at least 2 Rare Remnants
6. Runes: Runes are a nice bonus but not crucial - just equip whatever you get and replace if something better drops
7. Reforges: Have a separate Reforge Loadout with PVP Reforges (dmg vs players, dmg taken from players, benefitial duration)
8. Magic Affixes: Get those PVP Affixes (dmg vs players, dmg taken from players, cooldown reduction, benefitial duration) on your Set Items
9. Legendary/Class Affixes: Depending on your class and playstyle (Tank, CC, Damage Dealer) focus on offensive or defensive affixes on your primary gear
10. Builds: Try out different PVP builds - you may loose more but at least you tried something different
1. Combat Rating:  Focus on getting your Combat Rating high enough so you can enjoy playing all PVE content
2. Essences: Get all Essences for your class and your Essence Mastery to Level 4.
3. Upgrades: Upgrade your Gear to Level 30 so you can get all 5 Reforge Bonus Attributes
4. Legendary Gems: Resonance is even less important - focus on upgrading damage dealing or buffing 2-Star Gems and some good 1-Star Gems (Berserker, Everlasting, Entropic, Blessed Pebble)
5. Damage: Maximize your damage output with different builds for different content and get the right (PVE) reforges on your gear
6. Familiars: Get 1-3 Familiars with the Utility Traits for Quality of Life Improvement while farming / if you can get it cheap a Broodtalon/Skitter with Lingering Wounds Passive Skill for DPS
7. Stats: Secondary Stats are less important in PVE content - but high Armor Penetration and a high Critical Hit Chance can help clearing content a lot faster
8. Fun: Just focus on the content you like (e.g. Towers / Dungeons / Open World) - dont stress if you miss out on an event or a daily / weekly task
9. Fun: If the game gets stale for you - Explore the option to class-change. For me personally is often like playing a new game everytime i change class
10. Loot: The game favors casual players. After a long period of playing, drops will almost stop, so take a break and continue later and loot will suddenly be better

You can easily change classes in DI. Every 24h you can choose to change (free of cost). If you dont like the class you can switch back to your last class even before the 24h period ends.
Changing classes does not mean you loose anything on your character. Progression, Gems, Stash, Items, Essences - nothing is lost
You just get randomly assigned new Essences (but with all the original attributes, affixes, enchantments, etc.) Your original essences are put in your inventory
Those new [Transfer] Essences cannot be salvaged at Zamina - if you dont want to keep them you have to destroy them.
